question: When did Mahatma Gandhi founded the All India Harijan Sevak Sangh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1932**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi founded the All India Harijan Sevak Sangh on 30th September 1932.
 
• The organization was established to work for upliftment and welfare of the socially and economically downtrodden section of the society, particularly the Dalit community, who were then referred to as Harijans, meaning "children of God".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, also known as **Mahatma Gandhi, was born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat, India**.
 
• During his time in **South Africa**, from **1893 to 1914**, he developed his political views, ethics, and political leadership skills.
 
• He introduced the term** "Satyagraha" (devotion to truth),** which signified nonviolent resistance as a means of protest.
 
• Upon returning to **India in 1915,** he joined the Indian National Congress, beginning his active involvement in India's fight for independence.
 
• He led numerous campaigns against the **British rule, including the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, the Salt March in 1930, and the Quit India Movement in 1942.**
 
• Gandhi adopted a simple lifestyle, which included wearing traditional Indian clothing, eating a vegetarian diet, and practicing daily meditation.
 
• He strongly advocated for unity between **Hindus and Muslims, which was a major issue in Indian politics at the time.**
 
• Gandhi was a major advocate for **untouchables (Dalits), whom he called Harijans or "children of god".**
 
• He worked to end social discrimination against them and campaigned for their civil rights.
 
• He was key in helping India achieve independence from British rule.
 
• India was officially declared independent at midnight on **August 15, 1947**.
 
• Unfortunately, Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated in **New Delhi **on **January 30, 1948, by Nathuram Godse, a radical Hindu nationalist.**
 
• **Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolent resistance inspired future human rights movements around the world, earning him the title "Mahatma", which means "great soul".**
